question: How do you think New Zealand Should Respond to AI as a Society?
intro: Our research team has identified policy responses that we think could help ensure a positive future for AI in New Zealand. Please choose your top three preferred policies.

options.title: Fund an Office for AI
options.description: Building national expertise in AI, the office will study the risks and opportunities AI poses so that it can make independent recommendations to the government. It will also collaborate with other countries on AI risks.

options.title: Require AI companies to provide reliable AI detectors
options.description: Make AI companies provide Kiwis with a free tool that lets us easily check if something was generated with their AI. This is already the case in the European Union.

options.title: Harden Our Infrastructure against Catastrophic AI Misuse
options.description: Through the direction of the central Office for AI, increase funding for biosecurity (to protect us from AI bioweapons) and cyber defense (to protect us from AI hacking).

options.title: Jobseeker 2.0 To Help People Who Lose Their Jobs Because of AI
options.description: Expand jobseeker to have targeted retraining packages for people in sectors of the economy disrupted by AI automation

options.title: Tax AI Work like Human Work to Slow Job Losses and Maintain Government Revenue
options.description: Shift taxation away from human labour, and towards AI consumption. Do this by adding a tax on companies' AI services (i.e ChatGPT, Claude). This would not apply to Kiwi-owned AI services.

options.title: Invest in AI Infrastructure as a Public Good
options.description: New Zealand should invest in publicly owned AI computers. This preserves control and privacy and ensures AI is built and deployed in line with our values.

options.title: Mandate Human Control Over all Critical Societal Functions
options.description: Pass a law legally mandating human oversight in all domains that are critical to the functioning of society (such as policymaking, medicine, law, engineering, teaching, etc).

options.title: Protect our Children From AI Companies
options.description: Similar to the social media ban, all AI chatbots, agents, and companions should be banned for children under 16. From 16 to 18, AI usage would be introduced only in educational contexts.

options.title: Allow Companies to Build AI Computers here in exchange for Access and Infrastructure Upgrades
options.description: We get priority access, both to the best AI they host, and the ability to train and host our own AI. They must also pay for local infrastructure upgrades to avoid disrupting residents.
